## _**2.11 -**_ **ADJUSTMENT STEPPER FUNCTION** 

The adjustment stepper function permits correcting the wear of the electrodes that affects the quality of the welds. When the diameter of the electrodes increases, so does the contact section between electrode and piece to be welded and consequently the welding current density decreases (Amperes/mm[2] ). If the same adjustment is maintained for the entire electrodes' life, the quality of the last spots carried out is poorer as compared to the first ones. In order to correct this event, the adjustment stepper function was introduced, also called "stepper". The operating principle is to gradually increase the adjustment as the diameter of the electrodes increases so that constant current density is maintained. 

In order to describe the trend of the adjustment during the electrodes' lifespan, a stepper curve is programmed. This curve is made up of one or more segments for each of which the operator programs the number of welds and the relevant increment of the adjustment parameter in percentage. 

Once programmed, the increment of the adjustment parameter is applied to all the weld programs that use the same tool number of the programmed stepper module. 

Limits, if used, increase by the same percentage, as well as the pre-weld., post-weld. and welding 2 adjustments and the energy value to be attained. 

During the welding process, it is possible to correct the stepper curve trend by changing the 

parameters determining its trend. 

**In order to begin a new stepper curve, reset the spot counter relevant to the stepper module to be cleared, that is to say the one relevant to the tool in which the electrodes' starting diameter was restored.** 

## _**SIMPLIFIED USE OF THE STEPPER FUNCTION (LINEAR STEPPER)**_ 

The present example is carried out considering the control unit set to IK WORKING MODE. Only tool 1 will be used and the only active stepper will be the one relevant to the parameter adjustment associated with stepper law number 1. 

The stepper function can be used in a simplified manner by programming a simple percent increment for a specific number of welding spots that are to be carried out with the same electrodes. 

The operator must know the service life of the electrodes in order to adjust these parameters. To do this run some welding tests with new electrodes before they are replaced. Under these two conditions the currents, required for carrying out the welding spots of the required quality, are assessed. The change in percent is calculated and then it is set in the control unit. 

The parameters that allow the carrying out of the stepper function are entered in the **STEPPER MENU** . The instructions for programming these parameters are outlined in the relevant paragraph. 

In the "simplified" stepper function use, always set N.TOTAL STEPS parameter to 1 (since there is only one segment to be programmed). Enter the number of welds to be carried out in parameter SPOTS 1. In practice, the foreseen service life of the electrodes. Enter the required percentage increase in parameter INCREMENT 1-L1.

## _**SERIAL COM.**_ 

The operator may choose whether to activate the serial data transmission port and how it is to be used, connect a printer (232) or connect the control unit to a data supervision network (485), or not to use this option (OFF). 

## _**NET ADDRESS**_ 

This parameter indicates the identifying address of the control unit when connected in the network, activating the aforesaid option. 

## _**OUT LOCK/END**_ 

This parameter is used to indicate the time for activation of the corresponding output, interlock (LOCK) or end of cycle (END). 

## _**LOW FORCE SQ.**_ 

This parameter is used for enabling the low-pressure squeeze function for pneumatic circuit welders that are equipped with this function. Its enabling adds the SQUEEZE parameter to the welding program. 

## _**FORGE**_ 

This parameter is used for enabling the forging for pneumatic circuit welders that are equipped with this function. Its enabling adds the FORGE DELAY parameter to the work program. 

## _**PROP. VALVE**_ 

This parameter is used for enabling the use of a proportional valve for pneumatic circuit welders that are equipped with this function. Its enabling adds the PRESSURE parameter to the work program. 

If the FORGE parameter is enabled too, then the FORG.PRESS. parameter is added to the work program. 

## _**PRESSURE RATIO**_ 

This parameter can be used to select the optimum bar/Volt ratio for the type of proportional solenoid valve that is to be employed. It works only if the PROP. VALVE parameter is enabled. 

Further pieces of information are described in the paragraph **INTERFACE FOR PROPORTIONAL VALVE** . 

## _**AUTORETAIN**_ 

This parameter allows disabling the AUTORETAIN cycle start signal. 

On setting the parameter on the OFF value, the working cycle is stopped the moment the cycle start signal is disabled and does not complete the welding time. This occurs even if the welding current is in its flowing phase. 

The welding time is always completed whenever the value is set to ON. 

This function is specifically to be used when the machine works with mechanical devices instead of pneumatic ones.

## **START 1-2 NC** 

When this parameter is set to ON it enables the normally closed inputs of the cycle start signals. This allows the starting of the welding cycle only in the presence of the double exchange contact, normally open that closes and normally closed that opens. 

When set to OFF, the control unit ignores the status of the two signals and the starting of the welding only depends on the status of the NO inputs. 

If set to RIC 7-8, the two NO inputs become program recalls from a functional point of view so as to extend the number of recallable programs directly through the inputs. 

## **BIC 1-2 NC** 

When this parameter is set to ON it enables the normally closed inputs of the cycle start signals. This allows the starting of the welding cycle only in the presence of the double exchange contact, normally open that closes and normally closed that opens. 

When set to OFF, the control unit ignores the status of the two signals and the starting of the welding only depends on the status of the NO inputs. 

If set to RIC 5-6, the two NO inputs become program recalls so as to extend the number of recallable programs directly through the inputs. 

## _**SEAM WELD MODE**_ 

This parameter is used to enable the function that adapts the control unit to seam welder specifications. The activation of the seam weld mode automatically deactivates the autoretain. Further information is supplied in the **SEAM WELD MODE** paragraph. 

## _**CASCADE MODE**_ 

This parameter allows reversing the output signal of the end cycle (END), that is to say from normally open contact to normally closed contact, to allow putting more control units in cascade. 

Check the proper paragraph for further information. 

## _**WELD – NO WELD**_ 

When the optional board code 50200 is installed, this parameter allows the operator to select the priority of the weld-no-weld control. 

When the parameter is set to INT, the running of the external WELD-NO WELD line is deactivated whilst the button on the TE700 control unit remains enabled. 

When the parameter is set to EXT, the running of the external WELD-NO WELD line on board code 50200 is active whilst the button on the front panel of the TE700 control unit is disabled. When the parameter is set to BOTH, both WELD-NO WELD controls are enabled: the one on the TE700 front panel and the external control line on the board code 50200. The two controls are in series therefore to switch the unit to NO WELD mode, simply set only one of the two controls to NO WELD mode whilst in order to switch the unit to WELD mode both controls must be switched to WELD mode. 

## _**DSP UPG PRESS**_ 

If key <+> is pressed when this parameter is selected, the operator can remotely activate the software upgrade procedure inside the inverter unit. The spot welder must not be off during the upgrade procedure. Any other operation during the upgrade procedure is prohibited and welds may not be carried out. In order to resume the running of the spot welder after the upgrade procedure, it must be turned off and then back on again once the procedure is finished.

This working mode  typology is usually applied to a manual welder, where the operator carries the welding spots out always in the same order but with different working parameters. This working mode prevents the operator from manually changing the program and, therefore, from diverting his attention away from the piece to be welded, from changing the foot-pedal or other cycle start device. 

However the operator must pay utmost attention during the process not to perform fewer spots than those programmed, overlapping spots or not in the same order. 

However, should any error occur in the sequence work mode, it is possible to repeat either the last or another welding spot or to go ahead avoiding certain spots. ## _**2.19**_ **– TIP-DRESSINGS** 

The tip-dressing function is the combination, in just one function, of the current linear stepper function coupled with the restoring of the electrodes original diameter. 

The current stepper function allows compensating the electrodes wear which affects the welding quality. When the electrodes diameter increases also the contact section between the electrode and the piece to be welded increases. Consequently, the welding current density (Ampere/mm[2] ) decreases. In order to compensate this phenomenon, the current adjustment is gradually increased according to the electrodes diameter increase so to keep a constant current density. 

The restoring of the electrodes original diameter is an operation which is usually carried out by means of a tool (dresser) allowing restoring the electrodes diameter, which worn out and increased during the production, to its initial working value. 

If the same current adjustment is kept all along the electrodes life or if the electrodes diameter is never restored to its optimal value, the last carried out welding spots will have a lower quality than the first ones. 

As a rule the electrodes dressing function is used in the presence of an automation that provides an interface between the weld control unit and the dresser. 

After it has been set, the current increment is applied to all the welding programs used. 

4 different electrode dressing parameterizations are available and each parameterization is associated with one of the four different welding tools available. In this way it is possible to manage the use and dressing of 4 different types of electrodes separately, taking into consideration, for the current increase, only the spots carried out by every single electrode. 

This menu allows programming the tip-dressing number to be carried out during the electrodes life. 

TIP-DRESSING    T1 >TOOLS N°          1 DRESSING        OFF DRESSING NUMBER  01

If the seam weld mode is active on setting the mode, the AUTORETAIN function will be automatically deactivated at the START inputs. If the operator does not accept the deactivation of the AUTORETAIN function it will not be possible to activate the seam weld mode. 

This function allows the operator to adapt the control unit to the requirements of a seam welder. Consequently, welding current is supplied either continuously or via parameter COLD 2 in pulse mode. 

On keeping the cycle-start command active, the control unit keeps repeating the time set in the WELD parameter to prevent the control unit from completing a long weld. time on cutting off the cycle-start command. We suggest using short weld times. 

The welding current is measured indifferently through pulse cycle, WELD and COLD T. 2 time combination, or through continuous cycle, WELD time only. 

In the seam weld mode, the EV3 output is used as a roller-start command instead of being used for the forging. 

On enabling the programming of the WELD 2 parameter, the operator may set not only the CURRENT parameter but also the CURRENT 2 parameter. During the welding operation it is possible to commutate between one set current value and the other using the WELD 2 input present on the INVERTER unit. If the COLD T. 2 parameter is other than zero, each time the two foregoing current values commutate, the COLD T. 2 is carried out. the COLD T. 2 parameter is equal to zero, the passage between two set current values will take place instantly. 

If Rogowsky was set in the **FEATURES INVERTER** menu as current sensor for the adjustment loop, the continuous weld cannot be carried out but only a pulsed weld with a COLD T. 2 greater than or equal to 8mS. 

If TA was set as current sensor for the adjustment loop, it will be possible to carry out even a continuous weld with COLD T. 2 equal to zero. 

According to the type of current adjustment loop, the available weld modes differ as outlined in the tables below. 

During the welding in the SEAM WELD mode, the value of the welding current and the conduction percentage of the power semiconductors are displayed in real time on the control unit. Said information is updated every 0.5 seconds both during the hot times and the cold times.

The machine may be stopped when a consecutive series of welds fall out of the regulated limits. The number of consecutive welds that cause the control unit to stop is adjusted through parameter STOP BAD SPOTS in the **SETUP MENU** (for the programming directions, see the relevant paragraph). 

SETUP MENU >STOP BAD SPOT T1 01 STOP BAD SPOT T2 00 STOP BAD SPOT T3 00 

This value may range from 0 to 15. On programming the value to 0, the function is disabled. As such, on exceeding the preset limits, this does not stop the welder. There are four STOP SPOTS parameters, one for each available welding tool, so as to be able to differentiate the max number of admissible out of limits spots for each tool used. 

## **It must be pointed out that in order to count the out of limits welds, they must be consecutive, one after the other. This is applicable to each tool used.**

## _**CHAPTER 7**_ **– WELDS COUNTER FUNCTION** 

The control unit is fitted with the same number of weld counters as the number of selected transformers or welding tools. As such, the operator can count the spots carried out with each welding head or with each different tool so as to manage the consumption of the electrodes and the current increases according to the spots carried out in actual fact by each electrode. During the process, the display shows the counter of the spots carried out by the transformer or tool associated with the last weld program used. The counters increase at each weld cycle carried out by the tool associated with the counter. The weld cycles carried out in NO WELD mode are not counted. 

The welds counter may be cleared when the control unit is in work configuration. 

PRG 001-         -T1 WELD 0200Ms E 00100J IRMS 020.00KA SPOT 12340  r 020.0% 

Reset by pressing the CLEAR key on the TE700 control unit front panel. In this case the following message is displayed: 

CLEAR COUNTER UP / DN TO SELECT: RESET COUNTER T1? <+> OK <-> CANCEL 

If only one welding transformer or tool was selected, then only the T1 counter can be reset. Press key <+> to reset the counter or key <-> to leave the counter value as it is. If a number higher than one was selected for the welding transformers or tools, use keys and in the foregoing screen either to choose which counter to reset or reset all the counters of the spots associated with the tools used. If more than one tool was used, press the CLEAR key to view the request for resetting the counter associated with the last tool used. Press key <+> to reset the selected counter or all the counters. Press key <-> to leave the counters value as it is and return to the work screen. 

The spots counters may also be reset through the external control line only if optional board code 50200 is installed. In this case the activation of the signal to change the electrodes resets the spots counter. If only one spots counter is available it will reset automatically but if multiple counters were activated, which counter is to be reset is selected with recall lines RIC1, RIC2 and RIC3 according to the following table. 

|RIC 1|RIC 2|RIC 3|FUNCTION|
|---|---|---|---|
|OFF|OFF|OFF|The counter associated with the last weld program used is reset.|
|ON|OFF|OFF|Counter number 1 is reset|
|OFF|ON|OFF|Counter number 2 is reset|
|ON|ON|OFF|Counter number 3 is reset|
|OFF|OFF|ON|Counter number 4 is reset|
|ON|OFF|ON|All 4 counters are reset.|

Recalls must be activated before the signal to change the electrodes energizes and must be kept steady until the signal to change the electrodes de-energizes.

## _**8.2 - END CYCLE**_ 

The END CYCLE signal indicates the end of the weld cycle. The output, which is an optoelectronic contact, closes at the end of the hold time and may last according to the following possibilities: 

1. active until the cycle-start signal is present 

2. active for 40 ms, if the cycle-start signal has already been deactivated 

3. active for the entire OFF TIME if programmed to other than zero 

4. active until any message or signal is deleted from the display 

## _**8.3 - LOCK**_ 

The LOCK signal indicates current activation during the weld cycle. The output, which is an opto-electronic contact, closes at the beginning of the weld. time. It may also be the pre-weld. or the rise of current, the duration of which entails all weld. times and all the active current rising and dropping times.

## _**CHAPTER 10 –**_ **DOUBLE STROKE FUNCTION** 

In addition to the 3 solenoid valves that are part of the work cycle, the control unit manages a fourth solenoid valve aside from the work cycle to command the double stroke, which is also called the approach stroke. 

The input (D.STROKE) enables the output of solenoid valve EV4, to control the DOUBLE STROKE, and keeps it enabled separately from the work cycle; the output remains enabled even when the WORK - PROGRAM key is switched to PROGRAM position. 

On turning on the machine, with input (D STROKE) active, the output is disabled. In this case, during the first welding the control unit activates solenoid valve EV4 (that switches the electrode from position "A" to position "B") before the work cycle begins. Then the programmed welding cycle is carried out, on the elapsing of a fixed time of 0.6 seconds. When the cycle is over, solenoid valve EV4 does not deactivate and the electrode remains in position "B" as shown in the figure below. 

**==> picture [397 x 297] intentionally omitted <==**

Later on, by keeping the input activated (D.STROKE), the work cycles will be carried out starting from position B. 

In order to disable the EV4 double stroke output, simply deactivate the input (D.STROKE); the output will be disabled at the end of the cycle only if the input is deactivated during the weld cycle. 

If the input is enabled during the weld cycle, the output will be enabled only on issuing the next cycle-start command.

## _**11.1**_ **- RS-232 SERIAL INTERFACE** 

The RS-232 serial expansion board, code 50214, permits the operator to connect the TE700 to a printer or a personal computer which must be fitted with a RS232 serial interface board, to document production data. The board interfaces with the control unit through a 6-pin connector and with the printer (or computer) through a standard female 9-pin connector. The 9-pin connector is wired as follows: 

|PIN 2|TRANSMISSION(TD)|
|---|---|
|PIN 3|RECEPTION(RD)|
|PIN 4|DTR(ALWAYS ON)|
|PIN 5|MASS(SIGNAL GROUND)|
|PIN 6|DSR(ALWAYS ON)|
|PIN 7|RTS|
|PIN 8|CTS|

For the connection with a 9-pin port of a PC, simply use a standard modem cable, that is to say do not cross wires 2 and 3. 

On connecting the control unit to a serial printer with a 25-pin connector, keep in mind that the serial ports of the printers have the following pin configuration: 

|PIN1|GROUND(FRAME GROUND)|
|---|---|
|PIN2|TRANSMISSION(TD)|
|PIN3|RECEPTION(RD)|
|PIN 4|TRANSMISSION REQUEST(RTS)|
|PIN 5|READY TO SEND(CTS)|
|PIN 6|DATA READY(DSR)|
|PIN 7|MASS(SIGNAL GROUND)|
|PIN 20|TERMINAL READY(DTR)|

The control unit does not perform any type of handshaking at the serial port. The printer's serial port must be configured with the following values: 

|SPEED|9600 BAUD|
|---|---|
|WORD LENGTH|7 BIT|
|PARITY|EVEN|
|STOP BIT|1|

The control unit runs the transmission at the beginning of the OFF TIME. It is important to point out that the time required to print data is approximately 20 ms and this time will be added to the set OFF TIME. 

A specific parameter, in the special functions menu, allows the operator to choose whether or not to activate the print. The following data is printed for each weld: 

- Welding program number. 

- Tool or welding head which the weld spot was carried out with. 

- Duration of the welding in mS. 

- Welding current in KA. 

- Conduction percentage of the RO power semiconductors. 

- Energy supplied during the welding operation (only if the electrodes voltage gauge is installed on the machine).

## **5.1 Switching on the machine** 

Switch on the device by turning the main switch to the ‘I’ - ON position. 

## **5.2 Starting the control system** 

When the machine is switched on, all the LEDs light up for a few seconds. 

The display shows the following information for 2 seconds: 

- The mains power frequency recognised by the system. 

- The control software version. 

- The active operating mode (A0 or A1). 

After switching on, if no errors or faults are detected, all the LEDs except the WELD TIME LED go off and the display shows the currently set time value. 

## **5.3 Selecting programs and setting welding parameters** 

## _**5.3.1 Setting the welding start mode**_ 

- Turn the knob until the WELD TIME function is activated (LED on). 

- Press the knob to enter edit mode. 

- Turn the knob to the minimum value. 

- Press and turn the knob once more to select the welding start mode: 

## _**5.3.2 Setting the welding time**_ 

- Turn the knob until the WELD TIME function is activated (LED on). 

- Press the knob to enter edit mode. 

- Turn the knob to adjust the welding time to the desired value. 

- Press the knob once more to confirm the selection. 

## _**5.3.3 Setting the welding current**_ 

- Turn the knob until the CURRENT function is activated (LED on). 

- Press the knob to enter edit mode. 

- Turn the knob to adjust the electrical current to the desired value. 

- Press the knob once more to confirm the selection.

- Turn the knob until the localised heating program is activated (LED on). 

- Press the knob to enter edit mode. 

- Turn the knob to adjust the electrical current to the desired value. 

- Press the knob once more to confirm the selection.

- Set the program or adjust the welding parameters as described in the "Selecting programs and setting welding parameters” section. 

- Hold the gun (2) properly by the handle. 

- Keeping the gun in a vertical position (90°), press the trigger (3) to start the welding. 

- The heating is done by moving the electrode around on the metal sheet while exerting slight pressure. (Make a circular motion at a constant speed, without stopping). 

- When the welding is started (by the trigger or automatically with the AUTOSTART function), the set current is supplied for a maximum of 4 seconds; if this time is insufficient to produce the desired heating, release the trigger and press it again. 

(See the attached image A8) 

- Fit the hook (2) to the slide hammer (3) as described in the "Fitting electrodes" section. 

- Insert the hook into the previously welded pull ring and pull the slide hammer weight back against the stop (3) until the surface reaches the desired shape. 

- When the work is completed, remove the accessory by tilting it to one side.

## **WALTHER CHANGER PRAEZISION TOOL CHANGER SET UP DEVICE** 

Walther Changer Praezision Tool Changer Set Up device whose details are as follows : 

Attached please find pictures of our tool changer set up device. This device may be used by our customer to facilitate teaching and programming of the tool changers during first installation and maintenance. 

It is very important that the tool plates are adjusted leveled in X & Y. Afterwards one of each plates are put on each halt of the tool changer before programming. The robot side teach plate is clamped with a screw on a guide bolt to remain attached when upside down. 

During programming both halves are brought together. 4 radial markings at 90° (see picture …3.jpg) have to match, the plates have to nearly touch and the programming is O.K. 

Afterwards compensate 2x30mm =60mm distance in programming when teach plates are taken away and connection of the tool changer will be smooth. 

1. When first teach/program the robot cycle make sure that the tool side is level in X & Y in the parking station. 

2. Put the robot side teach ring on the robot side like shown in the attached picture and clamp it with the clamp screw on the robot side tool changer 

3. Put the tool side teach ring on the tool side like shown in attached picture 

4. Move the robot and bring the teach plates together parallel, face to face 

5. Make sure the 4 radial markings at 90° (see attached picture) match between robot side teach plate and tool side teach plate on all sides 

6. Compensate 60mm teach plate height towards tool side and you have the exact tool change location.

## **Safety Precautions Specified** 

## ![DANGER ] 

Always follow the instructions below in order to prevent bodily injuries. 

1. This product has been designed with enhanced safety in mind. You are requested to strictly follow directions given in this document. Failure to do so may result in a fatal or serious injury. 

2. Follow the local laws and codes as well as in-house rules when installing incoming and outgoing power supply units, selecting the installation site, storing products after welding, and disposing of wastes. 

3. Keep any unauthorized person off the location where the welder is operating or the job site as a whole. 

4. Do not allow anyone with a pacemaker implanted to come near the welder in operation or the job site until approval is given by the physician in charge. During operation, the welder is generating a magnetic field which adversely affects the pacemaker. 

5. Refer the installation, maintenance, and repairs of the welder to the qualified engineer or the person who has sufficient knowledge of the machine. 

6. For safety’s sake, make sure that the person who can understand the information contained in this manual and is technically competent is operating the welder. 

7. Never use this welder for purposes other than welding. 

8. Use the welder in the environment where easy access to the machine cannot be made by children, persons with precarious mentality, or animals in order to preclude the possibility of their being caught in the machine or involved in accidents, such as an electric shock. 

## ![DANGER ] 

To avoid incurring an electric shock, observe the following directions. 

**==> picture [52 x 44] intentionally omitted <==**

   - ＊ Contact with live parts other than the secondary conductor may induce a fatal electric shock or burns. 

   - ＊ Simultaneous contact with both ends of the secondary conductor may induce an electric shock. 

1. Keep clear of live parts other than the secondary conductor. 

- 2 Refer the qualified person to the job of grounding the welder according to the local regulations and codes. 

Be sure to connect the enclosure ground terminal of the equipment to the ground. 

If there are leaks with grounding job undone, the operator can be exposed to an electric shock or incur a serious injury. 

3. Do not start installation or maintenance until at least 5 minutes has elapsed after all incoming power switches in the switchbox have been turned off. 

4. Do not use cables of insufficient capacity, with scratched surfaces, or with exposed conductor. 

5. Securely connect the cable and properly insulate the connection. 

6. Do not operate the welder with the casing or the cover removed.

7. Do not wear broken or wet gloves. Always use dry, insulated ones. 

8. Periodically perform inspection and maintenance. Do not operate the welder until any damaged portion has been repaired. 

9. Use coolant of high quality, which has a resistance of more than 5000 Ω ・ cm and is almost free of sediments. 

10. Select the cable, compressed air hose, and water hose that are durable enough to withstand the specified load and pressure. 

11. Disconnect the power from all the units when the welder is to be off for an extended period of time. 

![DANGER] Do not put your fingers or hand between the electrodes.

＊ Placing any upper extremities of your body between the electrodes or in the moving parts of the gun can cause them to be pinched or caught, resulting in broken bones or other injuries. 

1. Ensure safety around the welder before turning on the power and supplying compressed air. 

2. When placing the welder out of use, turn off the power to the entire system and coolant lines. 

3. Avoid placing any upper extremities of your body between the electrodes or in the moving parts of the gun. 

CAUTION Wear protective equipment to protect yourself and your co-workers ! against splashes, spatters and loud noise that are generated during welding operation 

＊ Splashes and spatters may hurt your eyes and/or cause burns. 

＊ Loud noise may cause hardness of hearing. 

1. Wear safety goggles to shield your eyes from splashes and spatters. 

2. Wear protective gloves, long-sleeves, and leather aprons. 

3. Install a protective screen around the job site so that your co-workers are not exposed to splashes and spatters. 

4. When noise is intolerably loud, use hearing protection equipment.

![CAUTION][   Strictly follow the directions given below to prevent occurrence of a fire ] or an explosion.

＊ Splashes and spatters generated during welding operation and a base metal that is still hot immediately after welding may cause a fire. 

   - ＊ Cables with poor connections may also cause a fire due to heat generated during conduction. 

1. Keep away combustibles so that splashes and spatters are not brought into contact with them. If such combustibles must remain there, cover them with a nonflammable sheeting. 

2. Refrain from engaging in welding in the environment where flammable gases prevail. 

3. Do not bring a hot base metal near combustibles immediately after welding. 

4. Securely tighten the cable connections for insulation purposes. 

5. Install a fire extinguisher near the job site in case of ignition. 

6. If you are welding where the flow rate of coolant is below the specified level or in a total absence of coolant, the machine will overheat, possibly resulting in equipment failure, a fire, burns, or other problems. Be sure to supply coolant at higher than the specified flow rate. It is recommended to install a sensor that monitors the flow rate of coolant and, if the rate is found to drop below that level, actuates the safety circuit that turns off power supply.

## **3. Operational Conditions** 

Operate the X2C servo gun under the following conditions only: 

- (1) Ambient temperature: 0 to 40ºC 

- (2) Where installed: Indoors 

- (3) Coolant quality 

The coolant supplied to the X2C servo gun shall have an electrical resistivity greater than 5000 Ω-cm. 

- (4) Coolant temperature 

When measured at the inlet port, its temperature shall be lower than 30ºC. 

- (5) Altitude: Not exceeding 1000 m. 

## **4. Robots in use** 

The use of this gun is allowable only when the robot’s top (where the gun is installed) has an acceleration of lower than 3 G. When subjected to the acceleration exceeding 3 G, the bracket may break down. 

## **5. Guarantee** 

Any component of the X2C servo gun may be replaced with a new one free of charge if it fails from the cause reasonably ascribable to the supplier within 12 months from the start of its operation, within 18 months from the date of final shipment, or before the spot count reaches 5 million, whichever is sooner. 

However, all costs incurred in relation to jobs of dismounting from and installation onto the machine, shipment of the components concerned, dispatch of our technical personnel, and such shall not be borne by the supplier.  Also, some “consumable” components do not qualify under this guarantee.  See 2 ． Replacement Parts and Maximum Spot Count Acceptable 

## **6. Transportation, Handling, and Storage** 

During any packing, transportation, or removal from packing material, please take special precautions to protect the transformer and servo actuator.  Any type of external load, shock, or excessive vibration may damage these components. 

During handling on site, take the same precautions with the transformer and servo actuator.  Do not drop the weld gun assembly.  If weld gun needs to be set on floor, table, or similar, use robot mount bracket as a base.  Use straps or bolts if necessary to secure. 

Any type of extended storage should be in a dry environment and temperature should not exceed 40 deg C. 

## **7. Installation** 

Follow robot and weld control manufacturer’s instructions for proper installation procedures.

## **1** `．` **Description of Basic Functions** 

Overview of the X2C servo gun 

The gun has been designed with the consideration given to reduction in weight, slim profile, no L/R components, modularity, and ease of maintenance, 

Its weight has been reduced drastically compared to any of its preceding models since it incorporates a new type of lightweight inverter transformer, a motor with a hollow shaft as well as arm and gun brackets of aluminum alloy. 

L/R components have been eliminated and the overall width of the gun has been reduced to help minimize interference. 

Some of the components are common to both the C-type and X-type guns.  Only one c-type and one x-type gun body assembly allow easy modifications to create different gun configurations. 

This manual applies to all X2C Series: 

1. Standard series:  Used for standard steel welding applications and rated up to 6000N of welding force 

      - a. V1.0:  Has casted gun head for holder at end of arm, and separate cooling manifold 

      - b. V1.5:  Has copper sleeve for holder in arm, and integrated terminal manifold 

      - c. V3.0:  Has arm spacers made from solid insul material, copper sleeve style arms, and integrated terminal manifold 

2. High Performance (HP) series:  Used for high pressure (rated up to 8000N) and high current steel 

   - welding applications, utilizing a larger 150 kva transformer 

3. Aluminum series: Used in aluminum welding applications. Rated up to 8000N and utilizes a heavy duty transformer capable of welding up to 52,000 A 

In order to ensure operational safety, you are requested to read this manual until you have fully understood the information contained in it. Keep this document in the designated place.

## **4** `．` **Electric Polarity** 

All the machines in this series have a negative polarity on the movable side (on the side of the drive unit). 

The aluminum welding transformer can be assembled in reverse, if the opposite polarity is required. 

## **5** `．` **Quick Guide to Replacement of Electrode Tip** 

In the case of the electrode tip marked with a consumption limit line, replace it with a new one when the line has disappeared during dressing. The allowance for tip consumption is 10 mm. To be specific, replace the tip initially 25 mm long when this length has been decreased to 15 mm. Use a tip puller when changing the tip. If struck with a hammer or other similar tool, the related bearing or ball screw may be damaged. 

Weld Face Diameter 

## ! CAUTION 

Do not try to strike the tip side with a hammer or other tool; otherwise the ball bearing may be damaged. 

> ! CAUTION 

When a tip is stuck to the panel, do not forcibly peel it off by operating the robot. 

> ! CAUTION 

When replacing the screw adapter, keep the point holder from turning. 

## ! CAUTION 

Protect the main body of the drive unit against water splashes. (In particular, properly position the slide surface of the drive section and the plug silencer so that they may not be exposed to splashes.)

## **1** `．` **Maintenance Guide (Periodical Inspections Procedure)** 

## **1-1 Non-Periodical inspections** 

- (1) Dress the tip face with a file or a special-purpose dresser when it has been deformed or excessively worn. Dress the face until it regains as near the initial shape as possible. 

- (2) The tip is allowed to wear to a maximum of 10 mm. When this limit is exceeded, replace it with a new one. 

- → See Section 5 in the operation manual. 

- (3) If any component has overheated above 70ºC. (Note that the temperature of the shunt and motor may be over this spec), check the water flow rate. 

- →See Section 4-1 in the maintenance manual. 

## **1-2 Daily** 

- (1) Check the coolant line for leaks. 

- (2) Check the power supply section for damage or signs of water splashes. 

   - →See Section 4-2 in the maintenance manual. 

- (3) Using a flow meter, make sure that coolant is properly flowing. 

- →See Section 4-1 in the maintenance manual. 

## **1-3 Weekly** 

- (1) Remove spatter and clean components of the gun. 

- (2) Re-tighten the bolt fastening the secondary conductor. 

- →See Section 4-4 in the maintenance manual. 

- (3) Make sure that a misalignment amount of the tip is within 0.5 mm. 

- (4) Check the shunt for breakage. Replace it when one fourth to third of it is broken. 

## **1-4 Monthly** 

- (1) Check the bolts on all components for tightening condition. 

   - Re-tighten them if necessary according to the specified torque values stated in the bolt tightening torque list (7) 

   - →See Section 7 in the maintenance manual. 

- (2) Check the spot position (Deflection: 1% or less of gun throat depth; slippage, 0.5 mm or less; misalignment amount, 0.5 mm or less). 

- (3) Visually check the spatter cover. 

- (4) Check the welding force. It should be within ±5% of the specified level. 

- (5) Check all rods for damage. 

## **1-5 Semiannually** 

- (1) Using a Megger Tester in the 500V or 1000V range, check the insulation resistance. →See Section 4-7 in the maintenance manual. 

- (2) Measure the coolant flow rate. 

   - →See Section 4-1 in the maintenance manual. 

- (3) Lubricate each component to lubrication requirements. 

   - →See Section 3 in the maintenance manual. 

- (4) Check the motor for unusual noise. 

   - →See Section 4-3 in the maintenance manual. 

- (5) Check the scraper seal (if C-Type gun). 

   - →See Section 4-3 in the maintenance manual.

## **4.  Section-to-Section Inspection** 

## **4-1 Cooling Circuit** 

4-1-1 Cooling Circuit for Standard and High Performance X2C 

The differential pressure between the inlet and the outlet shall be less than 2.0 bar with the minimum necessary flow rate staying at 12 L/min or more. The flow rates required for all circuits are at least as follows: 

|Transformer|6.0 L/min or more|
|---|---|
|Gun body (arm on the stationary side)|3.0 L/min or more|
|Movableyoke(arm on the movable side/point holder)|3.0 L/min or more|

- Note: Certain adapter designs may not be able to reach 3.0 l/min of water flow.  In these cases, the duty cycle and/or weld current should be limited accordingly. 

## 4-1-2 Cooling Circuit for Aluminum X2C 

The differential pressure between the inlet and the outlet shall be less than 2.0 bar with the minimum necessary flow rate staying at 15.5 L/min or more. The flow rates required for all circuits are at least as follows: 

|Transformer|7.5 L/min or more|
|---|---|
|Gun body (arm on the stationary side)|4.0 L/min or more|
|Movableyoke(arm on the movable side/point holder)|4.0 L/min or more|

Connect a flow meter to each circuit and measure the flow rate of coolant running through it. If the flow rate or the difference in pressure between the inlet and the outlet fail to reach the levels indicated above, parts of the weld gun may overheat, possibly resulting in premature failure of gun components or poor welding / no weld conditions. 

## ! CAUTION 

For any type of high level maintenance (i.e. replacement of major components), it is recommended to remove the weld gun from the robot and perform the maintenance procedure in a designated area with additional work space and clearance.  Simple maintenance (greasing, cap adapter changes, wear checks, etc.…) can be performed with the weld gun on the robot.  Move gun to ‘maintenance position’ to perform these types of maintenance procedures.  Ensure proper space as designated by the appropriate plant personnel.

## **4-5 Disassembly** 

- When the gun must be disassembled, first remove spatter, oil, dirt, dust, and other foreign matter from all surfaces. 

- Before disconnecting the hose, remember the orientation of IN/OUT water lines and all components for ease of later reassembly. 

- While disassembling the secondary conductor, exercise care not to let small parts, such as insulators, bolts, and nuts as well as tools, fall into any line enclosures. 

- When removing the arm, mark its location so electrode alignment will not be changed when reinstalling it later. 

- Be careful not to damage the electrical surface areas. 

- The drive unit cannot be disassembled. 

## **4-6 Reassembly** 

- Before starting reassembly of the parts, ensure all parts are thoroughly clean and wipe moisture from their surfaces. 

- Make sure the electrical areas are free of problems, such as discoloration and oxidation. 

- Perform reassembly at a clean location, using care to avoid getting foreign matter into the product. 

- Apply conductive grease (such as Penetrox from Nagara Denshi) with a wire brush, coat the conductive areas where aluminum and copper alloy parts come into contact with each other and then mate them. 

## ! CAUTION 

The motor body in the drive unit, the direct-acting plain bearing, and the piston rod are final assembled after their alignment is ensured. 

**Therefore, the motor alone cannot be removed from the drive unit for replacement. In case of failure, replace the drive unit in its entirety.**

## **4-7 Insulated locations** 

Using a Megger Tester, check each insulated location for insulation resistance at regular intervals. The gun is insulated from the robot in the case of the X2C servo gun. Likewise, the secondary circuit in the welding transformer (arm, point holder, etc.) and the drive unit are insulated from other sections. If insulation fails, resulting in their shorts (contact), an unexpected problem will occur since welding current is allowed to flow via the servo motor ground cable. 

To check gun insulation from fixed arm to body, the fixed side terminal must be removed. Likewise, to check gun insulation from movable arm to body, the shunt must be removed. 

## **Also, it is critical to add a jumper wire between the positive and negative secondary transformer terminals to prevent damage to the diode.** 

Apply 500V between the fixed arm and the gun body. The result should be 1 Meg-Ohm minimum 

Apply 500V between the movable arm and the gun body. The result should be 1 Meg-Ohm minimum

- (1) The socket head screws have a categorized strength of 12.9, while the bolts, 10.9.

- (3) Use a low-strength adhesive (ex. ThreeBond 1344) for bolted connections, excluding secondary current connections, arm clamper bolts, and protective covers.

## ! CAUTION 

Never try to correct a deformed shape of any portion or the whole body of the gun by heating it using a gas burner or other heat source. If corrected in such a manner, the strength of the specific area will considerably be lowered, possibly leading to breakage of the gun itself because its major components are made of aluminum alloy.
